notes: §1985:VI.3.4.3 SR1 states for the DATE-COMPILED paragraph the rule §1985:VI.3.2.1.2 SR1 states for all five comment-entry paragraphs: "The comment-entry may be any combination of the characters from the computer's character set. The continuation of the comment-entry by the use of the hyphen in the indicator area is not permitted; however, the comment-entry may be contained on one or more lines." The first and third requirements conform at 85: CommentEntryOf opens the paragraph at the Area-A word DATE-COMPILED (CommentEntryParagraphs) inside an IDENTIFICATION DIVISION and keeps it open over every following line with no Area-A word; ConvertLine writes the header as the word and two periods (CommentEntryHeader, parsed as dateCompiledParagraph with no commentEntry) and discards each body line before the lexer reads it, so no character of the entry is scanned and the entry runs over as many lines as it likes (probed at 85: a DATE-COMPILED entry with periods inside it and a second line compiles). The text stage has no edition arm; the paragraph is refused from 2002 by its removal gate. The part not implemented is the prohibition: CommentEntryOf's first statement answers a continuation line (hyphen in the indicator area) inside an open comment-entry as one more body line, so a DATE-COMPILED entry continued with a hyphen is discarded as commentary and the program compiles with no diagnostic. The witness runs a DATE-COMPILED entry of special characters over two lines. No kb/Work note has the defect; it is the one mechanism of rule 1985-SR-VI.3.2.1.2-1.

next.reason: 1985: "The comment-entry may be any combination of the characters from the computer's character set."; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the DATE-COMPILED paragraph; no candidate covers its comment-entry.". No 2023 clause holds the DATE-COMPILED paragraph. The wording candidates cover SPECIAL-NAMES, PICTURE, PROGRAM-ID and PAGE, not this comment-entry, so the feature is dropped.
